html:
The Thaayorre are an Aboriginal people of the southwest of Cape York Peninsula in Queensland, living mainly at Pormpuraaw, which began as the Edward River Mission in 1938.

Their language, Kuuk Thaayorre, is famous among linguists. It has no words for left and right in the usual sense; speakers place everything by the compass, saying for example that a cup is to the northeast of a plate. Studies of Thaayorre speakers have been used to argue that language shapes how people think about space and time.

Their neighbours on the map include the Wik peoples to the north, the Kunjen to the south and the Koko Bera nearby. See Aboriginal Australian societies.
